::: {.callout-important}
## Conclusion in one paragraph

The 16,699 contigs that the BLAST/LCA step assigned to *Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus*
(taxid 3064049) are **not viral**. They are also **not endogenous viral elements**:
none of them encodes any detectable jingmenvirus protein. Every nucleotide hit lands on
the first ~286 bp of the GenBank reference records, upstream of their coding sequence.
That ~222 bp region is a **tick genomic interspersed repeat**. It occurs in ~11,000
copies across these contigs, in highly diverse flanking contexts. It is almost
exclusive to *Haemaphysalis* (32 of 34 samples; 10,425 of 10,988 copies). The reference
"MAG" records were assembled with Trinity from *Haemaphysalis longicornis* RNA-seq.
They appear to be **chimeras**: tick repeat (positions ~1–222) fused onto the front of a
genuine viral segment (from ~position 225 onwards). So the virus–tick junction we set out
to find exists, but it is in the reference sequences, not in our contigs.
:::

# Background and question

The LCA step assigned contigs from many samples to *Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus*, a
segmented, positive-sense RNA virus (*Flaviviridae*-like jingmenviruses). Our libraries
were made from **DNA extracts** (without RNase treatment), so an RNA virus should be
under-represented or absent. The hypotheses tested here:

1. **Real virus.** The contigs are viral RNA carried through the DNA extraction.
2. **Endogenous viral element (EVE).** Viral sequence integrated into the tick genome.
   We would expect viral coding sequence flanked by tick DNA, with a visible junction.
3. **Something else.** For example a mis-assigned tick sequence.

Lines of evidence used:

- contig length vs viral-hit length;
- co-occurring tick hits in the existing BLAST records;
- where the hits fall on the reference genomes;
- protein-level (tblastn) search for viral genes;
- copy number, position and flank diversity of the shared element;
- distribution across tick genera;
- comparison of the element with the Jingmen tick virus RefSeq.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Set-up: paths, tool locations and plotting helpers"
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

ROOT <- "/data/hb-austick/work/AlexG_data/Barker_ticks/microbe_analysis/old_analysis"
CJV  <- file.path(ROOT, "extracting_pathogens/Cheeloo_Jingmen-like_virus")
W    <- file.path(CJV, "are_these_real")          # all intermediate files land here
dir.create(file.path(W, "ncbi"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Bash chunks inherit these. BLAST+, cd-hit and python3 come from the base
# miniforge install; seqkit is the system copy.
Sys.setenv(ROOT = ROOT, CJV = CJV, W = W,
           PATH = paste("/data/hb-austick/work/miniforge3/bin", "/usr/bin",
                        Sys.getenv("PATH"), sep = ":"))

col_main <- "#014B87"   # CSIRO Ocean Blue
col_alt  <- "#E87721"   # CSIRO Orange
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                plot.title.position = "plot"))
rd <- function(f, ...) read.delim(file.path(W, f), check.names = FALSE, ...)
```

# How the contigs were assigned

Upstream, every SPAdes contig was searched with `blastn` (megablast, the default task)
against NCBI nt (2025-05-04 snapshot), using `-max_target_seqs 10 -evalue 1e-5`
(`code/blast.slurm.sh`). An LCA was then computed per contig. The script
`extract_cheeloo_jingmen.sh` pulled every contig with LCA = taxid 3064049, together with
**all** its BLAST hits (not only the viral ones).

::: {.callout-note}
`-max_target_seqs 10` matters here. When 10 near-identical viral reference records
out-score a tick hit, they take all 10 slots, so the tick hit never gets reported. A
**missing** tick hit in these records is therefore weak evidence. A **present** tick hit
is informative.
:::

```{bash}
#| label: show-extract
#| code-summary: "The extraction script and the upstream BLAST command"
cat "$CJV/extract_cheeloo_jingmen.sh"
echo; echo "---- code/blast.slurm.sh (BLAST call) ----"
sed -n '/^  blastn/,/evalue/p' "$ROOT/code/blast.slurm.sh"
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-table
#| code-summary: "Per-sample extraction summary"
summ <- read.delim(file.path(CJV, "summary.tsv"))
cat(sprintf("%d samples, %s contigs, %s bp, %s BLAST hits\n", nrow(summ),
            format(sum(summ$n_contigs), big.mark = ","),
            format(sum(summ$total_bp), big.mark = ","),
            format(sum(summ$n_blast_hits), big.mark = ",")))
kable(arrange(summ, desc(total_bp)), format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The first warning sign is the scale. A complete jingmenvirus genome is ~11 kb across four
segments, yet single samples carry up to **3 Mb** of "viral" contigs.

# Contig length vs viral-hit length

For each contig, the script below takes the union of query intervals hit by
Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus subjects (`jingmen_bp`), the union hit by any other subject
(`other_bp`), and the part of the latter that lies outside the viral interval
(`other_only_bp`).

```{bash}
#| label: per-contig-coverage
#| code-summary: "Per-contig viral vs non-viral hit coverage (python)"
cd "$W"
cat "$CJV"/blast/*.tsv | grep -v '^qaccver' > allhits.tsv
awk -F'\t' '$7=="3064049"' allhits.tsv > jhits.tsv

python3 - <<'EOF'
import collections, re
J = "3064049"
q = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"j": set(), "o": set(), "ot": set(), "samp": None})
# allhits.tsv has no sample column; recover it from the per-sample files instead
import glob, os
for f in glob.glob(os.environ["CJV"] + "/blast/*.tsv"):
    s = os.path.basename(f).split(".Cheeloo")[0]
    for ln in open(f):
        if ln.startswith("qaccver"): continue
        a = ln.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        qs, qe = sorted((int(a[11]), int(a[12])))
        d = q[(s, a[0])]
        if a[6] == J: d["j"].update(range(qs, qe + 1))
        else:
            d["o"].update(range(qs, qe + 1)); d["ot"].add(a[4])
with open("contig_cov.tsv", "w") as o:
    o.write("sample\tcontig\tlen\tkmer_cov\tjingmen_bp\tjingmen_frac\tother_bp\t"
            "other_only_bp\tj_start\tj_end\tother_taxa\n")
    for (s, c), d in q.items():
        L = int(re.search(r"length_(\d+)", c).group(1))
        cov = float(re.search(r"cov_([\d.]+)", c).group(1))
        jb = len(d["j"])
        o.write("\t".join(map(str, [s, c, L, cov, jb, round(jb / L, 4), len(d["o"]),
                len(d["o"] - d["j"]), min(d["j"]) if d["j"] else 0,
                max(d["j"]) if d["j"] else 0, ";".join(sorted(d["ot"]))])) + "\n")
print("contigs written:", len(q))
EOF
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-len-vs-hit
#| fig-cap: "Contig length vs the length covered by Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus hits. The dashed line is y = x (a contig entirely covered by viral hits). Viral hits never exceed 656 bp, however long the contig."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
cc <- rd("contig_cov.tsv") |>
  mutate(tick = ifelse(other_bp > 0, "Also has a non-viral (mostly tick) hit",
                       "Viral hits only"))
ggplot(cc, aes(len, jingmen_bp, colour = tick)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(col_alt, col_main), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Contig length (bp, log)", y = "bp covered by viral hits (log)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: len-bins
#| code-summary: "Viral fraction of contig, by contig length"
cat(sprintf("Viral hit span: median %d bp, max %d bp. Contig length: median %d, max %s bp.\n",
            median(cc$jingmen_bp), max(cc$jingmen_bp), median(cc$len),
            format(max(cc$len), big.mark = ",")))
cc |>
  mutate(length_bin = cut(len, c(0, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, Inf), dig.lab = 6,
                          right = FALSE)) |>
  group_by(length_bin) |>
  summarise(n_contigs = n(),
            median_viral_fraction = round(median(jingmen_frac), 2),
            with_nonviral_hit = sum(other_bp > 0)) |>
  kable()
cc |> arrange(desc(len)) |> head(15) |>
  select(sample, len, kmer_cov, j_start, j_end, jingmen_bp, other_only_bp, other_taxa) |>
  kable(caption = "The 15 longest contigs: a ~200 bp viral hit inside contigs of up to 25 kb")
```

The viral hit is a short, stereotyped ~200–222 bp block. The longer the contig, the
smaller the fraction it covers. That is what we would expect if a short element sits
inside longer genomic sequence, not from viral genomes.

# Co-occurring tick hits in the existing BLAST records

```{r}
#| label: tick-hits
#| code-summary: "Non-viral subjects on the same contigs"
ah <- read.delim(file.path(W, "allhits.tsv"), header = FALSE, quote = "")
names(ah) <- strsplit("qaccver saccver stitle sseqid ssciname scomname staxid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore", " ")[[1]]
nv <- filter(ah, staxid != 3064049)
cat(sprintf("%d of %d contigs (%.1f%%) also have a non-viral hit; %d have >=50 bp of non-viral hit outside the viral interval.\n",
            sum(cc$other_bp > 0), nrow(cc), 100 * mean(cc$other_bp > 0),
            sum(cc$other_only_bp >= 50)))
nv |> distinct(qaccver, ssciname) |> count(ssciname, sort = TRUE, name = "n_contigs") |>
  head(15) |> kable(caption = "Non-viral taxa, counted once per contig")
nv |> distinct(qaccver, stitle) |> mutate(stitle = substr(stitle, 1, 90)) |>
  count(stitle, sort = TRUE, name = "n_contigs") |> head(10) |>
  kable(caption = "Most frequent non-viral subject records")
```

About 6% of contigs also hit tick sequences, mainly a single *Dermacentor silvarum*
predicted mRNA (annotated "inositol polyphosphate 1-phosphatase"). The *Myotis* bat
chromosome hits come from a few contigs and were not followed up. Given the 10-target
cap, this 6% is a lower bound.

# Where the hits fall on the reference genomes

```{bash}
#| label: fetch-refs
#| code-summary: "Fetch the 38 reference records (FASTA, GenBank, CDS proteins) from NCBI"
# The nt snapshot used for BLAST is not mounted on this machine, so the public
# records are fetched from NCBI E-utilities. Cached: only fetched if absent.
cd "$W"
cut -f2 jhits.tsv | sort -u > jrefs.ids
ids=$(paste -sd, jrefs.ids)
E="https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=nuccore"
[ -s ncbi/jrefs.fa ]   || curl -s "$E&id=$ids&rettype=fasta&retmode=text"        > ncbi/jrefs.fa
[ -s ncbi/jrefs.gb ]   || curl -s "$E&id=$ids&rettype=gb&retmode=text"           > ncbi/jrefs.gb
[ -s ncbi/jprot.fa ]   || curl -s "$E&id=$ids&rettype=fasta_cds_aa&retmode=text" > ncbi/jprot.fa
# Jingmen tick virus RefSeq, all four segments, as an independent reference
J="NC_024111.1,NC_024112.1,NC_024113.1,NC_024114.1"
[ -s ncbi/jmtv.fa ]      || curl -s "$E&id=$J&rettype=fasta&retmode=text"        > ncbi/jmtv.fa
[ -s ncbi/jmtv_prot.fa ] || curl -s "$E&id=$J&rettype=fasta_cds_aa&retmode=text" > ncbi/jmtv_prot.fa
echo "reference records: $(grep -c '>' ncbi/jrefs.fa)"
echo "reference lengths: $(seqkit fx2tab -n -l ncbi/jrefs.fa | awk -F'\t' '{print $NF}' | sort -n | sed -n '1p;$p' | paste -sd- )"
grep -m1 -A2 "^REFERENCE   1" ncbi/jrefs.gb; grep -m1 "Assembly Method" ncbi/jrefs.gb
grep -m1 '/host=' ncbi/jrefs.gb; grep -m1 '/mol_type=' ncbi/jrefs.gb
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-subject-pos
#| fig-cap: "Where on the reference records the ~88,000 viral hits fall (subject coordinates), against the CDS starts annotated in those records (each record has two: glycoprotein at ~270–490 and VP1b at ~1,650–1,860). No hit reaches a coding sequence."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
jh <- read.delim(file.path(W, "jhits.tsv"), header = FALSE, quote = "")
jh$s_lo <- pmin(jh$V14, jh$V15); jh$s_hi <- pmax(jh$V14, jh$V15)
gb <- readLines(file.path(W, "ncbi/jrefs.gb"))
cds <- as.integer(sub("^\\s+CDS\\s+(complement\\()?<?(\\d+).*", "\\2",
                      grep("^\\s+CDS\\s", gb, value = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Viral hits: n = %s; subject coordinates %d-%d. Earliest annotated CDS start in any reference: %d.\n",
            format(nrow(jh), big.mark = ","), min(jh$s_lo), max(jh$s_hi), min(cds)))
# The global ranges overlap slightly (286 vs 271), so test each record against
# its OWN first CDS start.
acc <- sub("^VERSION\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", grep("^VERSION", gb, value = TRUE))
rec <- cumsum(grepl("^VERSION", gb))
keep <- rec > 0                                    # drop LOCUS..DEFINITION lines before 1st VERSION
first_cds <- tapply(seq_along(gb)[keep], rec[keep], function(i) {
  l <- grep("^\\s+CDS\\s", gb[i], value = TRUE)[1]
  as.integer(sub("^\\s+CDS\\s+(complement\\()?<?(\\d+).*", "\\2", l)) })
per_ref <- jh |> group_by(acc = V2) |> summarise(max_hit_end = max(s_hi), n_hits = n()) |>
  left_join(data.frame(acc = acc, cds_start = as.integer(first_cds)), by = "acc") |>
  mutate(gap_to_cds = cds_start - max_hit_end)
cat(sprintf("Records where any hit reaches that record's own CDS: %d of %d. Smallest gap between hit end and CDS start: %d bp.\n",
            sum(per_ref$gap_to_cds <= 0), nrow(per_ref), min(per_ref$gap_to_cds)))
pos <- bind_rows(data.frame(x = jh$s_hi, what = "End of viral hit on reference"),
                 data.frame(x = cds, what = "Annotated CDS start"))
ggplot(pos, aes(x, fill = what)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 20, boundary = 0, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~what, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_alt, col_main), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Position on reference record (bp)", y = "Count")
```

All 38 records are *MAG: Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus* entries, assembled with Trinity
from *H. longicornis* RNA-seq (Ye et al. 2024, *Microbiome* 12:35). Each one covers
only the glycoprotein/VP1b segment. Every one of our hits lies in reference positions
1–286. Within each record, the last hit ends at least 195 bp before that record's first
CDS. **None of our contigs matches the viral coding sequence at the nucleotide level.**

# Do any contigs encode jingmenvirus proteins?

This is the decisive test. Any real virus, or any EVE large enough to be called viral,
should show protein similarity. The queries were:

- the glycoprotein and VP1b proteins from all 38 reference records;
- all proteins from the four segments of the Jingmen tick virus RefSeq (NS5-like
  RdRp, NS3-like helicase/protease, glycoprotein, capsid), which are the most
  conserved jingmenvirus proteins.

These were searched with tblastn against all 16,699 contigs, with low-complexity
filtering off.

```{bash}
#| label: tblastn
#| code-summary: "tblastn of jingmenvirus proteins against every assigned contig"
cd "$W"
F="$CJV/fasta"
if [ ! -s all_cjv.fa ]; then
  for f in "$F"/*.fasta; do
    s=$(basename "$f" .Cheeloo_Jingmen-like_virus.fasta)
    seqkit replace -p '^' -r "${s}|" "$f"          # prefix sample name to contig id
  done > all_cjv.fa
  makeblastdb -in all_cjv.fa -dbtype nucl -out cjvdb > /dev/null
fi
seqkit stats -T all_cjv.fa
cat ncbi/jprot.fa ncbi/jmtv_prot.fa > allprot.fa
echo "query proteins:"; grep '>' allprot.fa | grep -o 'protein=[^]]*' | sort | uniq -c
OF='6 qseqid sseqid pident length qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore'
tblastn -query allprot.fa -db cjvdb -evalue 1e-3 -seg no -outfmt "$OF" -num_threads 2 > tbn_strict.tsv
tblastn -query allprot.fa -db cjvdb -evalue 10   -seg no -outfmt "$OF" -num_threads 2 > tbn_loose.tsv
echo "hits at e <= 1e-3: $(wc -l < tbn_strict.tsv)"
echo "hits at e <= 10:   $(wc -l < tbn_loose.tsv)"
echo "best five hits at e <= 10:"; sort -t$'\t' -k9,9g tbn_loose.tsv | head -5
```

There are **zero** hits at e ≤ 1e-3. The best hit even at e ≤ 10 is e = 0.17 over 30
amino acids, which is noise. No contig encodes recognisable jingmenvirus protein. That
rules out a real virus, and it rules out an EVE in the usual sense (integrated viral
coding sequence).

# What is the shared element?

Positions 1–300 of OR114895.1 (the most-hit record) were taken as a probe. It was
searched against all contigs with sensitive `blastn -task blastn` and no hit cap.

```{bash}
#| label: element
#| code-summary: "Map the 5' reference region onto all contigs"
cd "$W"
seqkit grep -r -p OR114895 ncbi/jrefs.fa | seqkit subseq -r 1:300 > elem.fa
cat elem.fa
blastn -task blastn -query elem.fa -db cjvdb -evalue 1e-5 -max_target_seqs 100000 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid slen sstart send qstart qend pident length' > elem_hits.tsv
echo "element copies: $(wc -l < elem_hits.tsv) on $(cut -f1 elem_hits.tsv | sort -u | wc -l) contigs"
echo "dust low-complexity intervals in the element:"; dustmasker -in elem.fa -outfmt interval | tail -n +2
```

```{r}
#| label: element-stats
#| code-summary: "Copy structure, probe end-point and position on contig"
eh <- read.delim(file.path(W, "elem_hits.tsv"), header = FALSE,
                 col.names = c("sseqid","slen","sstart","send","qstart","qend","pident","length"))
eh <- eh |> mutate(lo = pmin(sstart, send), hi = pmax(sstart, send),
                   at_end = lo <= 20 | hi >= slen - 20)
kable(count(count(eh, sseqid), n, name = "n_contigs") |> rename(copies_per_contig = n))
kable(head(count(eh, qend, sort = TRUE), 5),
      caption = "Most common end-point on the probe: the element ends at reference position ~222")
cat(sprintf("Copies touching a contig end (within 20 bp): %d of %d (%.0f%%)\n",
            sum(eh$at_end), nrow(eh), 100 * mean(eh$at_end)))
```

The homology stops sharply at reference position **222** (and at 208/221 in related
copies). That is a clean boundary. About 73% of copies sit at a contig end, which
typically happens when a repeat breaks the assembly graph.

## Flank diversity: one locus, a tandem array, or interspersed?

If the element is a single locus, or a tandem array, its flanks will all be the same.
If it is an interspersed repeat (for example a SINE or another transposable element),
the flanks will vary. The 150 bp immediately upstream of each copy (strand-aware) was
extracted and clustered at 90% identity.

```{bash}
#| label: flanks
#| code-summary: "Extract upstream flanks and cluster with cd-hit-est"
cd "$W"
python3 - <<'EOF'
seqs, name = {}, None
for l in open("all_cjv.fa"):
    l = l.strip()
    if l.startswith(">"): name = l[1:].split()[0]; seqs[name] = []
    else: seqs[name].append(l)
seqs = {k: "".join(v) for k, v in seqs.items()}
comp = str.maketrans("ACGTNacgtn", "TGCANtgcan")
seen = set()
with open("lflank.fa", "w") as o:
    for l in open("elem_hits.tsv"):
        c, slen, ss, se = l.split("\t")[:4]
        ss, se = int(ss), int(se)
        if c in seen: continue                    # one flank per contig
        if ss < se and ss > 150:                  # element on + strand
            f = seqs[c][ss - 151:ss - 1]
        elif ss > se and ss + 150 <= int(slen):   # element on - strand
            f = seqs[c][ss:ss + 150][::-1].translate(comp)
        else: continue
        seen.add(c); o.write(f">{c}\n{f}\n")
print("flanks extracted:", len(seen))
EOF
cd-hit-est -i lflank.fa -o lflank_c90 -c 0.9 -n 8 -T 2 -M 4000 -d 0 > /dev/null
echo "clusters at 90% identity: $(grep -c '^>Cluster' lflank_c90.clstr)"
echo "largest clusters:"; awk '/^>Cluster/{if(n)print n; n=0; next}{n++} END{print n}' lflank_c90.clstr | sort -rn | head -5 | paste -sd' '
echo "singleton clusters: $(awk '/^>Cluster/{if(n)print n; n=0; next}{n++} END{print n}' lflank_c90.clstr | awk '$1==1' | wc -l)"
```

The flanks are highly diverse. 3,035 flanks form ~1,500 clusters, and ~1,050 of those
are singletons. **The element sits in many unrelated genomic contexts: an interspersed
repeat.** One large cluster (~800 flanks, about a quarter) shares a common upstream
sequence. That probably marks a sub-family in which the ~222 bp element is the 3′ part of
a longer repeat unit. It is worth classifying (see *Further tests*).

# Distribution across tick genera

```{r}
#| label: fig-genus
#| fig-cap: "Copies of the element, by tick genus (sample genus from metadata/sample_metadata.tsv). Labels show samples with the element / samples sequenced."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
md <- read.delim(file.path(ROOT, "metadata/sample_metadata.tsv"))
copies <- eh |> mutate(sample_id = sub("\\|.*", "", sseqid)) |> count(sample_id, name = "copies")
gen <- md |> select(sample_id, tick_genus, tick_species) |>
  left_join(copies, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(copies = coalesce(copies, 0L),
         tick_genus = ifelse(is.na(tick_genus) | tick_genus == "", "(unrecorded)", tick_genus))
gtab <- gen |> group_by(tick_genus) |>
  summarise(samples = n(), with_element = sum(copies > 0), copies = sum(copies)) |>
  arrange(desc(copies))
kable(gtab, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
ggplot(gtab, aes(reorder(tick_genus, copies), copies)) +
  geom_col(fill = col_main, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", with_element, samples)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Element copies across all samples")
gen |> filter(copies > 0, tick_genus != "Haemaphysalis") |> arrange(desc(copies)) |>
  kable(caption = "Non-Haemaphysalis samples carrying the element")
```

The element is essentially **Haemaphysalis-specific**, and the reference MAGs also come
from a *Haemaphysalis* species (*H. longicornis*). The single unrecorded-genus sample (`8267`) with
~550 copies should be checked: it may well be a *Haemaphysalis*. The handful of copies in
*Amblyomma* and *Ixodes* samples could come from a related element, or from low-level
cross-sample carry-over.

```{r}
#| label: no-element-samples
#| code-summary: "LCA-assigned samples in which the element probe finds nothing"
summ |> filter(!sample %in% copies$sample_id) |>
  left_join(select(md, sample_id, tick_genus), by = c("sample" = "sample_id")) |>
  kable(caption = "LCA-assigned samples with no copy of the OR114895 probe")
```

```{bash}
#| label: no-element-hits
#| code-summary: "What those contigs hit on the reference records"
cd "$CJV"
for s in $(tail -n +2 summary.tsv | cut -f1); do
  grep -q "^$s|" "$W/elem_hits.tsv" && continue
  tail -n +2 blast/$s.Cheeloo_Jingmen-like_virus.blast.tsv
done | awk -F'\t' '{lo=($14<$15)?$14:$15; hi=($14<$15)?$15:$14; print $2"\t"$7"\t"lo"-"hi}' |
  sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10
```

These samples are mostly *Bothriocroton*. Their contigs hit a single record (OR114906.1),
at positions ~14–108. That is again the non-coding 5′ region, upstream of the viral CDS,
so it is probably a divergent copy of the same repeat (or a related one) that the
OR114895 probe misses at e ≤ 1e-5. They are artefacts of the same kind.

# The junction is in the reference records

If positions 1–222 of the reference are tick repeat, then the true viral sequence should
begin just after it. The jingmenvirus segment termini are conserved, so the probe was
compared with all four Jingmen tick virus RefSeq segments.

```{bash}
#| label: junction
#| code-summary: "Compare the probe with Jingmen tick virus RefSeq segments"
cd "$W"
echo "probe vs Jingmen tick virus RefSeq (all hits, e <= 10):"
blastn -task blastn -query elem.fa -subject ncbi/jmtv.fa -evalue 10 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid pident length qstart qend sstart send evalue'
echo; echo "probe vs the 38 Cheeloo references (e <= 1e-10): alignment length distribution"
blastn -task blastn -query elem.fa -subject ncbi/jrefs.fa -evalue 1e-10 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid pident length sstart send' | awk '{print $3}' | sort -n | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -6
```

Probe positions 1–222 have **no** similarity to any Jingmen tick virus segment.
Probe positions ~225–260 match the **extreme 5′ ends** of JMTV segments 2–4
(e.g. 14/14 nt identity to segment 4, positions 21–34). That is the conserved
jingmenvirus segment terminus. The reading of each Cheeloo reference record is therefore:

```
 1                    ~222 ~225                ~290-490                          ~2,750
 |---- tick repeat ----|    |-- viral 5' UTR --|==== glycoprotein / VP1b CDS ====|
     (what all our contigs hit)    ^ conserved jingmenvirus terminus
```

This suggests the records are **assembly chimeras**: a *Haemaphysalis* repeat transcript
joined onto a genuine viral segment by Trinity, in RNA-seq from the same tick species.
The terminus match is short, so this junction position is well supported but not proven.
Mapping the original reads (SRR24769044 for OR114895) onto the record would test it
directly (see below).

# Conclusions

1. **Not a virus.** No contig encodes jingmenvirus protein. Hits are confined to a
   non-coding ~222 bp region.
2. **Not an EVE or retrovirus.** There is no viral coding sequence, no long-terminal
   repeat signal, and no viral protein. What we see is a tick repeat, not virus-derived
   DNA in the tick genome.
3. **A *Haemaphysalis* interspersed repeat.** It has ~11,000 copies, diverse flanks,
   frequent contig-end positions, matches to tick genomic and transcript sequences, and
   is restricted to *Haemaphysalis*.
4. **Reference contamination is the root cause.** The GenBank *Cheeloo Jingmen-like
   virus* MAG records carry this repeat at their 5′ end, so megablast + LCA calls every
   *Haemaphysalis* sample "Jingmen-positive".

::: {.callout-warning}
## Implications for the pipeline
These LCA calls should not be reported as virus detections. Options:

- mask positions 1–~286 of the 38 OR1148xx/OR1149xx records (or drop the records) before LCA;
- require that any viral call is supported at the protein level (blastx/DIAMOND or
  tblastn), which would also catch other reference-chimera artefacts;
- treat absence of non-viral hits cautiously, because `-max_target_seqs 10` hides them.
:::

# Further tests (not yet done)

- **Read-level support in the reference.** Map SRR24769044 onto OR114895 and look for a
  coverage step, or a lack of spanning read pairs, at ~position 222–225.
- **Read-level support in our data.** Map reads back to the long contigs and confirm
  read pairs span the element–flank boundaries. This rules out an assembly artefact on
  our side.
- **Coverage ratio.** Compare depth over the element with depth over its flanks. A
  collapsed repeat shows inflated depth.
- **Repeat classification.** Search the element against a *H. longicornis* genome
  assembly and Dfam, or run RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker, to name the repeat family
  (e.g. SINE, tRNA-derived).
- **Sliding-window homology.** This is no longer needed for boundary-finding, because
  the HSP coordinates already give a sharp boundary. It would still be useful for
  visualising individual long contigs.
- **Wet lab.** RT-PCR vs no-RT PCR on RNA for genuine jingmenvirus segments, and
  junction-spanning PCR on DNA.
